title: No source names a service owner for the run of any of the 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Slide 3 Service levels, Owner column; slide 6 Decision needed, DL02; slide 15 Who owns what
description: Version 2 makes the application owner the owner of a severity 1 and leaves the identity open in DL02 (the Tribe lead, with the ACE team as technical custodian). The realignment makes 19 services, each with its own schema, topic and task queue, so a run book needs one owner per service. The Ownership Map v1 assigns tables, endpoints, events, workflows and jobs to the service codes P1 to P10 and S1 to S9 but names no service owner, and Template and Rules R5.3 gives a suggested team by work type only. Version 3 therefore states the service code as the owner in the map and leaves the run-time owner open where it is needed.
evidence: Version 2 slide 3: 'Severity 1 ... Owner: Application owner'; slide 6: 'DL02 | Who the application owner is | The Tribe lead, with the ACE team as technical custodian'; the Services sheet of the Ownership Map v1 gives code, service, name, wave, schema, REST base, topic and queue, with no service owner column; Template and Rules R5.3 gives TechX, ACE team, SCB IT infrastructure, DevOps team and QA team as suggested owners by work type; R3 default rulings name owners for parameters and reference data, the case list API, the rule registry, the interaction ledger and feature flags only.
proposed: Name one service owner role for each of the 19 services, record it on the Services sheet of the Ownership Map next to the work-type suggestion, and close DL02 at the same time.

title: The tier 2 and tier 3 roles of version 2 are not defined per service now that there are 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Slide 2 Who runs the Workbench after go-live; slide 15 Who owns what
description: Version 2 gives tier 2 as the platform administrator, the reference data administrator and the data steward, and tier 3 as the TechX recovery squads and the ACE team, without saying which person or which team serves which service. The target has 19 services with their own schema, login, queue and topic, so a support request has to land on a named role for the service concerned. No source read for this deck gives that mapping, so version 3 keeps the tier table of version 2 and leaves the per-service role open.
evidence: Version 2 slide 2: 'Tier 2 ... Platform administrator; reference data administrator; data steward' and 'Tier 3 ... TechX recovery squads; ACE team'; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service its own schema, login, task queue and Schedules; the Rulings sheet of the Ownership Map v1 names P3 rwb-case for parameters and reference data and P7 rwb-decision for the rule registry, but no tier role for a service.
proposed: State, for each tier, the role that serves each service, for example one platform administrator per wave, and print that role on the service's run book page.

title: Version 2 gives four severity bands but no alert threshold, no SLO and no dashboard per service
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Slide 3 Service levels; slide 9 Run book per service, step 1
description: Version 2 fixes a respond time and a restore time for four severities and nothing else. A run book per service needs the signal that starts the clock on that service: an error rate, a consumer lag, a dead-letter count or an outbox age. Architecture v5 gives the health and metrics endpoints, the retry topics and the dead-letter alert, and ADR-023 makes observability per service, but no source read gives a threshold, an error budget or a dashboard per service, so version 3 uses the four severity bands and leaves the threshold open.
evidence: Version 2 slide 3 gives respond and restore times only, with no threshold; Architecture v5 slide 20: 'REST /health, /metrics for the platform'; slide 22: 'retry topics 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, then .dlt + alert'; no source read gives an alert threshold, an SLO, an error budget or a named dashboard for any of the 19 services.
proposed: Publish one alert and dashboard page per service, with latency, error rate, consumer lag, dead-letter count and outbox age, and cite it from the service's run book page.

title: No source gives an on-call rota per service or the hand-off from the tier roles to the 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Slide 4 Hours and shifts; slide 16 Hours, rota and on call, per service
description: Version 2 has business hours with tier 1 and tier 2 on duty, an early shift for the data steward and outside hours with SCB IT on call for severity 1 and the platform administrator on call by rota. It gives one rota for one deployable. The target has 19 services in waves 1 to 4, so the rota and the hand-off point from tier 1 to the service concerned have to be stated per service. No source read for this deck states either, so version 3 keeps the four rows of version 2 and adds the per-service column with the open value.
evidence: Version 2 slide 4: 'Outside hours | SCB IT on call for severity 1; platform administrator on call by rota'; slide 5 gives four escalation rows and no rota; the Services sheet of the Ownership Map v1 gives the wave of each of the 19 services but no rota; no source read names a paging tool, a rota period or a hand-off point.
proposed: Publish one rota page per service for business hours, the early shift and outside hours, and state the point at which tier 1 hands a request to the service's owner.

title: The source deck carries no change log, no version history and no tool line
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2
section: Slide 19 Change log; slide 7 What changed in version 3
description: Version 2 is six slides and has no change-log slide, no revision table and no tool line. The cover carries the date 28 October 2026 and the file properties carry no version history, so the rows before version 2 cannot be reconstructed from the source. Version 3 keeps the cover date, records version 2 as the source row and states the gap rather than inventing the history.
evidence: The converted text of the version 2 file has six slides: cover, who runs the Workbench, service levels, hours and shifts, escalation and the DL02 decision; none is a change log and none carries a tool line; the cover reads 'Henka Group, 28 October 2026'.
proposed: Keep a change-log slide in every later version and rebuild the rows of versions 1 and 2 from the file properties and the release record.

title: The source deck has no run book per service, although the target has 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Slides 8 to 17, the run book per service
description: Version 2 describes one operating model for one deployable: tiers, service levels, hours, escalation and the DL02 decision. It never names a service, a schema, a topic, a task queue or a scheduled job, so nothing in it tells a person on call what to look at for the service that is failing. Architecture v5 gives each service its own contract, topic, task queue and Schedules, and the realignment run requires a run book per service. Version 3 adds the pages on slides 8 to 17 and records the gap here.
evidence: The version 2 deck has six slides and names no service; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 give the IN and OUT contract of every service, each with its own schema, topic and queue rwb-<short>; slide 20 note: 'Every service: built from one template ... its own Schedules'.
proposed: Keep one run book page per service beside that service's contract story, and review it at the start of the service's wave.

title: No approval of version 3 is recorded and the source deck carries no status
source: Recovery Workbench Run Operating Model v2
section: Slide 7 What changed in version 3, status note; slide 19 Change log
description: The source has no status line and no approval record, and the realignment run takes no approval stop. Version 3 therefore carries the status Draft, states that no approval is recorded, and leaves the approval open here and in the assumption row.
evidence: The version 2 deck has six slides and none has a status, an approver, a sign-off line or a date of approval; the run rules in AGENTS.md rule 9 forbid waiting for an approval and require an assumption instead.
proposed: Record the approval of version 3 by the programme, the solution architect and the ACE team, with a date, and keep a status line on the cover and in the change log of every later version.
